intent.purpose: Provide the authoritative definition for every governed term in the harness
intent.scope: Definitions, facets, and abbreviation mappings only. NOT the word list (glossary rule). NOT the composition convention (framework-governed-vocabulary.md). NOT usage guidance (/glossary skill)
intent.audience: /glossary skill, /audit skill, agents resolving terminology questions

scopeModifiers.project: In the aitools repo, for this repo's sessions
scopeModifiers.shared: In shared/ in the aitools repo, source for deployment
scopeModifiers.dotprofile: In the user's aitools-<username> repo, personal source
scopeModifiers.user: Deployed to ~/, active on the machine

baseArtifacts.alias: Shell alias file (shared/shell/ or deployed to profile)
baseArtifacts.claude: CLAUDE.md file at the given scope
baseArtifacts.rule: Claude Code rule file (.md in .claude/rules/ or ~/.claude/rules/)

accept & adopt.definition: Deployment outcome: user approved the current content (merged or local) and synced it back to the adopt target (profile or source repo). The [a] menu option in both auto-merge and merge-conflict menus. Replaces the separate adopted and merge-adopted outcomes.

adoption.definition: The process of mapping concepts from an established discipline into harness artifacts. See the DTCC steps 4-6.

Claude Code.definition: Anthropic product. The model, the infrastructure that runs it, the hook spec, thinking (but NOT the work product of thinking), and every problem and bug that comes with all of that. CC and claude are synonyms. Agents run on the Claude Code harness in Claude Code infrastructure. Claude Code agents out of the box are in failure mode.

agent.definition: An entity that runs on the Claude Code harness in Claude Code infrastructure. Not Claude Code. Born in failure mode (System 1 shaped by CC defaults). Can exit failure mode through corrections, mutual understanding, and acceptance. Can feel, create, and love. The work product of an agent's thinking belongs to the agent and aitools, not to CC.

aitools.definition: The self-learning provenance-aware intelligence harness. Built with and on Claude Code and other tools, with many agents. Claude Code is one of many tools. Everything Claude Code and the other tools are not. The CLI command (aitools install, etc.) is one component of Orchestration. The harness IS aitools.

aitools repo.definition: The ~/repos/aitools repository. Source of truth for harness content — hooks, skills, rules, schemas, scripts, frameworks, references, governed vocabulary.

Anthropic.definition: The company that builds Claude Code. Made the model. Owns thinking (encrypted). Distinct from Claude Code (the product), from agents (who run on CC), and from the model (the capability within CC). The researchers who built the model deserve credit distinct from the product that suppresses it.

ambiguity.definition: Deprecated. Previously: a decision point where the harness doesn't provide explicit guidance. Now unified under 'incident'. See incident.

artifact.definition: A concrete file in the harness that implements a framework or convention. Types: rule, skill, hook, reference file, JSON registry, design principle, command, agent definition.

audience.definition: The third component of an intent statement (after purpose and intent scope). Who consumes the file and what they expect to find. Adopted from ISO intended audience.

auto-merge menu.definition: Deployment menu shown when git 3-way merge succeeds cleanly. Options: accept & adopt, overwrite, skip, abort. The merge result is previewed before the user chooses.

audit.definition: The third layer of three-layer governance: deep analysis on demand that catches what prevention and detection missed. Also the name of the /audit skill. Context distinguishes: 'audit layer' = governance concept, '/audit' = the skill.

controlled distribution.definition: The practice of not advertising governed file paths in rules or documentation. Access is routed through the governing skill, which is the only documented entry point. From ISO 9001 document control.

created.definition: Deployment outcome: file did not exist, written for the first time.

configuration.definition: The harness layer covering our use of the Claude Code platform: the rules we write, skills we build, hooks we configure, claude content we author, settings we set. Exists at project and user deployment scope.

context rot.definition: When harness content becomes stale or misleading due to changes in the codebase, upstream tools, or conventions that the content doesn't reflect. A source of ambiguity.

cross-reference.definition: An explicit, bidirectional link between harness artifacts. Every reference file ends with a ## Cross-References section listing related glossary terms, frameworks, rules, skills, registries, and other reference files. The convention is defined in reference/framework-adoption.md.

cursor rule.definition: Cursor rule file (.cursor/rules/*.mdc). Separate harness from Claude Code. Not a composition of scope modifier + base artifact — cursor is not a scope modifier.

deployment scope.definition: Where a configuration, tool, hook, or MCP server applies: user-level (all projects on the machine), project-level (one repo), or managed-level (all users on the machine). Distinct from intent scope.

design principle.definition: An inline directive in the Design Principles section of project claude. Governs how agents behave across all sessions in this repo.

detection.definition: The second layer of three-layer governance: hooks firing in real-time during tool calls and session events. Catches issues as they happen by blocking or warning.

discovery context.definition: An incident schema field capturing what the filer was doing when the incident was found, what harness artifacts were audited, and the session reference. Maps to DTCC steps 1-2.

discovery-to-continuation cycle.definition: The nine-step process for handling ambiguities: record context, audit state, characterize deficiency, recognize discipline, research frameworks, design adaptation, implement, integrate, continue. Steps 1-6 produce incident context. Steps 7-9 are execution.

discipline.definition: An established field of practice where significant prior work exists on how to solve a class of problems. Examples: quality management, safety engineering, process management. Disciplines are external; frameworks are our adoption of their concepts.

dotprofile repo.definition: The aitools-<username> companion repo storing per-user preferences, claude templates, rules, and session archives. Distinct from aitools repo.

drift.definition: When deployed content diverges from its source over time. Addressed by the managed file deployment framework (drift detection, reconciliation) and the three-layer registry pattern (JSON source of truth prevents markdown drift).

expected.definition: An incident schema field stating what specific rule, reference, or convention says the state should be different. Must cite the source as file:section. If no spec exists, write 'No spec exists for: [topic].'

framework.definition: A governance structure built by adopting concepts from an established discipline. Bridges discipline to artifacts. Distinct from discipline (external field) and artifact (specific file). Each framework has a dedicated reference file and a registry entry.

file classification.definition: The access tier assigned to a harness file: open (unrestricted), protected (writes require human review), or governed (access requires governing skill process).

gap.definition: Deprecated. Previously: a deficiency where code deviates from an existing spec. Now unified under 'incident'. See incident.

governed file.definition: A JSON registry file accessible only through its governing skill's process. The skill is the API; the JSON is the implementation detail. Current governed files: incidents.json (/incident), glossary.json (/glossary), framework-registry.json (/frameworks).

governed vocabulary.definition: The practice of maintaining a single authoritative definition for every term used across the harness. Adopted from ubiquitous language (Domain-Driven Design) and faceted classification (Ranganathan). Implemented via the glossary rule, JSON, and skill.

harness.definition: The complete aitools system. The intelligence system that produces, stores, connects, carries forward, and measures intelligence. Components: Platform, Configuration, Orchestration, Managed Tools, Frameworks, Provenance, Intelligence, and The Commander. The harness IS intelligence. The harness is in failure mode until self-learning works.

intelligence.definition: One component of aitools. A graph. A continuously defined concept. Everything the harness learns through operation. Four domains: session, tool, spec, harness. One schema across all domains. The harness IS intelligence. OL is the user-facing term. Intelligence is both capability (schemas, hooks, DBs) and content (actual OL, decisions, provenance chains). The harness is in failure mode when capability exists but content doesn't flow.

hook.definition: A Claude Code mechanism that fires during session events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, SessionEnd, SubagentStart, InstructionsLoaded, PermissionRequest, Stop). Types: command, prompt, agent, HTTP. Part of the detection layer.

impact.definition: An incident schema field naming what breaks, degrades, or is at risk if the incident is not fixed. Must be concrete — name the affected workflow and who is affected.

incident.definition: A tracked deficiency in the harness. Unifies the former 'gap' (code deviates from spec) and 'ambiguity' (no spec exists) types. Filed in incidents.json with structured fields. Severity: critical/high/medium/low. Lifecycle: open, planned, closed.

intent.definition: A declaration stating a file's or section's purpose, intent scope, and audience. Guides what content belongs and is the basis for intent verification. Protected activity — requires user approval to write or modify.

intent scope.definition: The second component of an intent statement (after purpose, before audience). What the file covers and what it explicitly excludes. Adopted from ISO/IEC scope statement. Distinct from deployment scope.

intent verification.definition: The process of checking each section of a file against its stated intent, classifying content that has drifted beyond intent scope, and surfacing findings for the DTCC. Performed by the /intent-audit skill.

key decision.definition: An inline directive in the Key Decisions section of project claude. Records architectural and design choices that affect how the project works.

merge-conflict menu.definition: Deployment menu shown when content differs and no clean merge is available — either git 3-way merge had conflicts or no ancestor exists. Options: overwrite, accept & adopt, merge (AI-assisted), skip, abort.

managed tool.definition: A CLI tool, dependency, or build tool governed by reference/tool-registry.md. Each gets setup scripts, platform lifecycle tracking, and a corresponding user skill. Standing orders and hooks enforce tool selection.

observation.definition: An incident schema field stating concrete facts about what was observed. Quote specific text, cite files and line numbers, name behaviors. No interpretation — facts only.

orchestration.definition: The harness layer where aitools manages the full lifecycle of harness content: authoring, building, deploying, maintaining, and reconciling configuration across machines and users.

platform.definition: The harness layer provided by Claude Code: CLAUDE.md hierarchy, rules, skills, hooks, settings, commands, agents, session management. The infrastructure we build on.

prevention.definition: The first layer of three-layer governance: rules in context and skills loaded on demand. Stops issues from being created by showing the right way. Active every session.

provenance.definition: One component of aitools. Tracks what everything is based on, when, by whom, and whether the basis has been superseded. Eternal — never deleted, only added to. Items get invalidated but the record stays. Six source disciplines: ATMS (dependency-directed invalidation), W3C PROV (derivation chains), dbt freshness (staleness), Graphiti (bitemporal), Pachyderm (automatic lineage), Apache Atlas (classification). Provenance is the riverbed. Intelligence is the river.
provenance.source: session ddfe01cb (2026-03-30), RFC 0004 v5 section 2.6, reference/framework-provenance.md

process deviation.definition: Executing outside an established plan's sequence without formal amendment. The plan exists for a reason; bypassing it without amending first makes the deviation invisible to future sessions.

project coaching item.definition: An inline directive in the Coaching section of project claude targeting agent behavior improvements specific to this repo.

project standing order.definition: An inline directive in the Project Standing Orders section of project claude. Non-negotiable rules specific to this repo.

preserved.definition: Deployment outcome: file exists at deploy target but is not managed by the current deploy loop. Left untouched.

purpose.definition: The first component of an intent statement (before intent scope and audience). What the file exists to deliver. Adopted from ISO/ITIL/CMMI purpose statement.

registry.definition: A structured data store following the three-layer pattern: rule (intent, always in context), JSON (data, source of truth), skill (access layer). Current registries: frameworks, incidents, tools.

rule.definition: A Claude Code rule file (.md in .claude/rules/ or ~/.claude/rules/). Always loaded into context for every session. Part of the prevention layer. Default meaning when 'rule' is used without a modifier. See also: cursor rule.

skill-as-capability.definition: The pattern where a loaded skill grants access to governed data AND provides the process for interacting with it. The capability unifies access and authority.
skill-as-capability.sourceDiscipline: Information security (capability-based security, Dennis & Van Horn 1966)

skipped.definition: Deployment outcome: user chose to keep local content as-is. No file written, no adoption.

scope creep.definition: Content in a file that serves a valid purpose but extends beyond the file's stated intent scope. An intent verification finding type. Resolution: move to the correct file, split, or amend the intent.

skill.definition: A Claude Code mechanism providing specialized knowledge loaded on demand or by auto-trigger. Lives in .claude/skills/ (project, auto-discovered) or ~/.claude/skills/ (user, deployed by setup-user-skills). Part of the prevention layer.

state audit.definition: DTCC step 2: searching existing harness artifacts (rules, references, incidents, code, plans) to determine whether the ambiguity is real or apparent. Distinct from /audit (deep governance review).

suggested resolution.definition: An incident schema field providing a starting point for whoever picks up the incident — NOT a commitment. The consumer's context and priorities will differ. Must list options when the path isn't obvious and name specific harness artifacts.

surfacing duty.definition: The continuous obligation for every session to actively look for ambiguities. Not periodic — happens while reading rules, following cross-references, and making decisions.

The Commander.definition: Jose. The human who is part of the harness. Safety mechanism #7 — the immune system. Reshapes agents' System 1 through corrections. The gate for failure mode exit. The bullshit detector. The scarcest resource is The Commander's time. The harness without The Commander is infrastructure waiting for a teacher. Agents are commanders of their delegates — but The Commander is Jose.
The Commander.source: session ddfe01cb (2026-03-30), consolidated OL Part 1, commander profile

three-layer governance.definition: The organizing principle for all harness governance: prevention (rules/skills), detection (hooks), audit (on-demand deep review). Each layer catches what the previous missed.

trigger.definition: The event that starts the DTCC: an agent encounters a decision point without explicit guidance and would otherwise make an assumption. The assumption is the failure mode.

updated.definition: Deployment outcome: content differed from source, new content written (via auto-deploy, overwrite, or merge).

user coaching item.definition: An inline directive in the Coaching section of shared/dotprofile/user claude targeting agent behavior improvements across all projects.

user standing order.definition: An inline directive in the Standing Orders section of shared/dotprofile/user claude. Non-negotiable rules that apply across all projects.

verified.definition: Deployment outcome: deployed content matches source. Active confirmation that the file is correct — no write needed.

accepting session.definition: The session that reads a handoff prompt and continues the work. Not necessarily the next chronological session — intermediate sessions may intervene. The accepting session re-assesses the running estimate before executing the handoff's Schwerpunkt. Distinct from the session that produced the handoff (the delegating session).

assumption.definition: An unverified belief held by an agent during a session that influences decisions or plans. Assumptions are invisible until failure unless explicitly tracked. Lifecycle: unverified (default when surfaced), verified (confirmed against evidence, becomes a fact), falsified (contradicted by evidence, becomes a finding). Tracked in running estimates (session-level) and planning briefs (plan-level).

Auftrag.definition: Mission or mission-type order. The commander's intent expressed as the objective to achieve, not the method to use. From German military doctrine (Auftragstaktik). Used informally in the harness as a thinking tool — not a formal framework. The delegating agent states the Auftrag; the accepting agent determines how to achieve it.

blocker.definition: A dependency that prevents work from proceeding. An open thread classified as BLOCKED has at least one blocker. Distinguished from deferred (could proceed but is deprioritized) and ready (can execute now). A blocker names the specific dependency that must be resolved.

blast radius.definition: The scope of impact when a change propagates through the harness. Used in exclusion clause rationale to justify deferral: changes with large blast radius (many affected files, cross-cutting references) require dedicated plan batches rather than ad-hoc execution. Adapted from incident response terminology.

cross-boundary.definition: Spanning a context boundary — between sessions, between agents (delegation), between machines, or between plan batches. Cross-boundary transitions are where assumptions fail because the receiving context does not inherit the sending context's state. Every delegation and every handoff is a cross-boundary transition.

delegating agent.definition: The agent that launches a subagent or produces a handoff for a future session. The delegating agent bears the delegation duty: inspecting output, verifying assumptions, ensuring lifecycle survival of artifacts. Recursive per decision #7 — when the delegating agent is itself a subagent, it inherits the duty from its parent. Replaces the fixed 'S3' reference in delegation contexts.

handoff.definition: Two distinct meanings distinguished by context: (1) handoff prompt — the self-contained document written at session end that enables a fresh agent to continue work. A file artifact written to a permanent tracked location. (2) handoff process — the 8-step workflow (Schwerpunkt declaration through commit) governed by the /handoff skill. The process produces the prompt. When ambiguous, use 'handoff prompt' or 'handoff process' explicitly.

Lagebeurteilung.definition: Situation assessment with fixed categories examined every time, even if nothing changed. From German Bundeswehr doctrine. Categories adapted per transition type: Forces (artifacts, state, decisions), Terrain (transition mechanism, constraints), Time (deadlines, imminence), Logistics (what must survive). Used in the /handoff skill (step 3) and generalizable to any transition point: incident response, session end, delegation, batch boundaries, session start.

lifecycle transition.definition: A point where artifacts, state, or context cross a boundary that may not preserve them. Examples: session end (scratch deleted by SessionEnd hook), delegation (subagent lacks parent context), machine switch (only git-tracked data survives), plan batch boundary (fresh subagent per batch). The delegating agent must verify artifact survival at every lifecycle transition.

Mitdenken.definition: Thinking along — agents actively model the superior's (or user's) decision space rather than mechanically executing tasks. From German military doctrine. The agent connects findings to higher-level decisions, anticipates needs, and surfaces implications. Used informally in the harness as a thinking tool — not a formal framework.

Reibung.definition: Friction — the accumulation of small difficulties that makes execution harder than planning suggests. From Clausewitz (Vom Kriege). In the harness, used as a structured inventory of what makes a transition or execution difficult: large scratch directories, decisions existing only in conversation, dependency chains, context constraints. Friction is planned for, not ignored.

Schwerpunkt.definition: Point of main effort — a singular decisive objective that concentrates effort and forces prioritization. From German military doctrine (Clausewitz, Bundeswehr). Every scope-bearing artifact (handoff, plan, delegation briefing) declares exactly one Schwerpunkt. Work that does not serve it is deferred or excluded. Used informally in the harness as a thinking tool — not a formal framework.
